answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashable if it joins a coordinated fake-review campaign. A reputation system then weights endorsements by bonded stake and limits how much one cluster can boost itself, using shared funding and behavior to detect likely coordination. An attacker cannot create influence for free: they must lock capital across many accounts, risk losing it when caught, and wait for the bond to be returned. Even a comet crossing an ocean would not make nectar a substitute for that costly commitment.
